purpose: The committed ceiling on explicit deferral. Nothing prevented a stream from adding a deferred route or scenario; 49/21 had been stable by convention alone. Three rules in `graph verify` read this file: `route-deferral-regression` and `scenario-deferral-regression` fail an id that is deferred and not named here, so adding a deferral needs an explicit bump in the same commit and becomes a reviewed decision instead of a diff nobody reads; `deferral-irreversible` fails an id listed in `retired`, so an id that has once left the floor can never come back as architecture debt. The ratchet is monotone non-increasing, not strictly decreasing: requiring the number to fall every release manufactures pressure to mount a route badly to make a number move.
regenerate: This file is committed and hand-edited, unlike `release/test-registry.json`. An id enters `routes` or `scenarios` only with the change that defers it, and leaves only with the change that mounts, deletes or un-defers it - moving it to `retired` in the same commit unless the contract deletes it outright.

routes.floorNote: The approved ceiling is 48 and stays 48; the ratchet is monotone non-increasing, so a tree that sits well under the ceiling does not lower it. The registry defers 21 today. Nineteen ids are still named in `deferred` below and are no longer deferred in the contract: the registry pointer lane mounted fifteen and the capacity lane mounted `account_get`, `workspace_current_get`, `workspace_limit_get` and `workspace_limits_list`, neither moving them out of this file. They stay listed here rather than moving to `retired`, because retirement is irreversible and is the mounting change's decision to make, not this merge's. The list is a ceiling, so naming an id that is no longer deferred only makes the ratchet slack, never wrong. `session_clone` left `deleting` because P0.2 deleted it from the contract outright, exactly as that entry instructed. Eleven ids are in `retired` because they were mounted rather than deleted - P1.1, P3.2 and P5.2 landed `session_restore`, `session_stop`, `session_trash` and `usage_query`; P3.4a landed the four upload routes; P3.3a landed `secret_put` and P3.3b `provider_credential_register`. `provider_credential_revoke` is retired with them: P0.1 deferred it because nothing composed ever registered a credential, and P3.3b made that premise false, so the deferral was withdrawn in the merge that brought P3.3b in. Re-deferring any of the eleven is a regression, not architecture debt. What remains deferred and belongs to P0.1 is `session_approval_get` and `session_approvals_list`: manual approval is out of launch scope by decision D4, `brain-mux` hardcodes an empty `approval_required`, nothing constructs `Write::PutApproval`, and `session_approval_respond` is still deferred - so both reads would return a confident empty page over data no producer writes, which is exactly what the `501` arm exists to prevent.

scenarios.floorNote: Every scenario but `SC-REGIONAL-ADMISSION` is deferred. `verify_release_candidate` already refuses an all-deferred registry, so this floor guards the other direction: a scenario that was runnable and is quietly deferred again.
